tts.affected_edges: ECP.permission.scope -> PD writable scope -> receiver handoff
tts.first_failing_invariant: validate_bundle accepts a self-consistent but rehashed permission expansion
tts.detail: An independently re-hashed record whose ECP.permission.scope was widened from src/** to ** still validates PASS with 0 findings, because content_hash proves the record is internally consistent and not that it agrees with the bound PD scope. No executor was invoked and no permission was actually granted; this is a contract-closure gap rather than an exercised escalation.
tts.close_condition: validate_bundle emits a SEMANTIC finding when an ECP permission scope is broader than the PD scope it is bound to, with POS/NEG fixtures
tts.close_criterion: validate_bundle emits a SEMANTIC finding when an ECP permission scope is broader than the PD scope it is bound to, with POS/NEG fixtures

tts.first_failing_invariant: non-record sidecar values are not validated
tts.detail: Injecting LOW_RISK_VERIFIED, independent_acceptance=PASS and allowed_claims=[PRODUCTION_VERIFIED] into PI-PKG._profile_meta validates with 0 findings, because the sidecar is stripped before schema validation by design. The compiled bundle emits NOT_ASSESSED and no LOW_RISK_VERIFIED, so the shipped artefact is correct; the risk is a consumer reading validation PASS as authority for sidecar values.
tts.close_condition: either declare a minimal schema for the sidecar or state in the consumer documentation that PASS never authorises sidecar values
tts.close_criterion: either declare a minimal schema for the sidecar or state in the consumer documentation that PASS never authorises sidecar values

tts.first_failing_invariant: an empty trace array is accepted
tts.detail: Setting a compiled PI trace to [] yields bundle PASS without a rehash. The schema now enforces array typing and the item required-keys, which is exactly what POST-F03 asked for; it does not require non-empty trace or cross-record closure. Reported as the observed limit of validate_bundle, not as an executor bypass.
tts.close_condition: add a minItems/cross-record closure rule for trace only if the upstream contract requires it, with POS/NEG fixtures
tts.close_criterion: add a minItems/cross-record closure rule for trace only if the upstream contract requires it, with POS/NEG fixtures

tts.affected_edges: wheel filename -> distribution METADATA -> tag -> README
tts.first_failing_invariant: preview.1 and preview.2 ship the same distribution version 0.1.0
tts.detail: Both prereleases are pipd_ls_sp-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl with different hashes, so pip upgrade/cache resolution and user support threads cannot distinguish them by version. The released tag is immutable and was NOT rewritten. The next patch must carry a PEP 440-legal version higher than 0.1.0 (e.g. 0.1.1b1 with tag v0.1.1-preview.1) with wheel name, METADATA, entry point, tag and README made consistent.
tts.close_condition: an owner-authorised successor prerelease ships a distinct distribution version, verified by an isolated-venv old->new upgrade, uninstall and rollback
tts.close_criterion: an owner-authorised successor prerelease ships a distinct distribution version, verified by an isolated-venv old->new upgrade, uninstall and rollback
